transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-26
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Cho (CTO, Everwave), Priya Singh (Head of Security, Everwave), Tom Alvarez (Infra Lead, Everwave)

Auto-generated sections (optional):
Summary: Initial security posture review focused on identity (SSO/SAML), encryption & KMS options, RBAC/audit logging needs, and retention requirements. Customer leaning toward private or dedicated for sensitive workflows; interested in HSM/KMS integration and per-tenant audit visibility.
Topics: SSO/SAML, SSO SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, key rotation, data retention, SOC2/ISO attestation, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.
Action items: see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. we're here to run through Evergreen — sorry, Everwave's security and hosting needs and see where Redwood fits. marco is with me for the technical bits.
[00:15] Daniel Cho: thanks lena, appreciate it. quick note, timezone math made my morning chaotic so i'm caffeinated.
[00:22] Marco Ruiz: cool, hi daniel, priya, tom. i'll try to be crisp, feel free to interrupt, especially on the KMS bits.
[00:30] Priya Singh: thanks, marco. high level, Everwave processes shipment manifests with PII; we have a compliance push next quarter — want to know if Redwood can meet our SOC2 bar and how keys and audit logs look.
[00:45] Tom Alvarez: also want to understand network topologies — can we run Redwood Private in our VPC behind a firewall? any on-prem air-gap options?
[00:58] Lena Park: totally. quick framing: Redwood has hosted (fast), dedicated (reserved GPU pool/backplane) and private (customer-managed control plane + optional on-prem bundle). we can map features to each. on SOC2/ISO, we are attested — we'll share the certs — but we need to walk through specific controls you care about.
[01:20] Daniel Cho: good. Priya, what are your must-haves?
[01:24] Priya Singh: must-haves are: SSO with SAML + SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC so only specific service accounts can call generate endpoints, full immutable audit logs with export/search, envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (CMKs), and a clear retention policy. also key rotation windows.
[01:45] Marco Ruiz: ok noted. on SSO we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning, SSO integrates with Okta, Azure AD, generic SAML IdPs. a few customers use our SCIM user sync and RBAC layer on top for per-team policies.
[02:10] Tom Alvarez: is RBAC enforced client-side or in the runtime? i.e., can we block certain models for a given team?
[02:16] Marco Ruiz: enforced server-side at the gateway — per-token and per-route permissions. you can limit model access per role, also create service accounts with token scopes. it's not just policy on the client.
[02:31] Priya Singh: can you audit that? we need to show who invoked what model and with what prompt (or at least prompts hashed) for incident response.
[02:39] Marco Ruiz: yes — audit logs capture request metadata, model id, route, token id, timestamps, and response latencies. we redact or hash prompt bodies by default for hosted SKU, but for Dedicated/Private we can keep plaintext logs in your controlled storage if that's a requirement — though we'll want to discuss data residency.
[03:05] Daniel Cho: interesting. data residency is a big red flag for us — certain manifests cannot leave our environment. can Redwood host entirely inside our AWS account or on-prem?
[03:16] Lena Park: Redwood Private is built for that: you run the inference nodes in your VPC, and optionally an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. control plane can be customer-managed in high security cases. for pure hosted, data flows through Redwood-managed infra in region(s) we operate — so that won't work for those manifests unless masked.
[03:36] Tom Alvarez: does Private support HSM integration? We use AWS CloudHSM for our master keys.
[03:42] Marco Ruiz: yes, Private supports KMS integrations. we have connectors for AWS KMS and CloudHSM, GCP KMS, and you can bring your own HSM if needed. keys are used to wrap model encryption keys and to encrypt audit logs at rest if you choose.
[03:59] Priya Singh: rotation policy: do you enforce automatic rotation or is that customer-controlled? what are rotation windows and how are old keys retired from token caches?
[04:10] Marco Ruiz: rotation is policy-driven. for Private, you control rotation; we support key versioning and rotation without taking nodes offline using a staged roll. we also manage KV cache invalidation: old wrapped keys are rotated and the runtime drops old KV entries after a TTL. specifics can be in the design doc we'll share.
[04:34] Daniel Cho: ok. SOC2/ISO — can you send the attestation and the last penetration test summary? legal will want those.
[04:41] Lena Park: yes, we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs and the latest pentest exec summary after this call.
[04:50] [05:00] Priya Singh: about audit logs — you said immutable. who stores them and how do you prevent tampering?
[05:08] Marco Ruiz: good question. for hosted, logs are stored in Redwood's logging cluster with WORM controls and retention policies. for Dedicated and Private, customers can ship logs to their S3 buckets or SIEM via syslog/forwarders; we support write-once append-only streams and signed log chaining to detect tamper. some customers run a separate ingestion pipeline into their own Elastic or Splunk.
[05:40] Tom Alvarez: does Redwood support per-tenant encryption keys? we want encryption separation per customer and per-environment.
[05:48] Marco Ruiz: yes. we can do per-tenant CMKs and per-environment wrapping keys. again, with Private you own the CMKs in your KMS; Dedicated can be configured with tenant-level keys depending on contract. hosted has multi-tenant models so we have a shared runtime but we can do envelope encryption with customer keys for data-at-rest separation.
[06:12] Daniel Cho: latency concerns — i assume Private will have lower egress latency because data stays local, but what about throughput? we have bursty loads during route cutoffs.
[06:22] Marco Ruiz: for throughput Dedicated gives predictable GPU pools and autoscaling policies; Private performance depends on your infra. we provide guidance on pooling and autoscaler configs tuned for bursty patterns. also our smart batching adapts to short bursts to keep latency SLOs while improving token economics.
[06:44] Priya Singh: for compliance we need retention windows per-data-class — can Redwood enforce automatic purge of logs and data after X days? and ensure deletion is irreversible?
[06:55] Marco Ruiz: yes. we have retention policies that can be per-route or per-model. for Private, we can enforce deletion workflows inside your environment — secure wipe of caches and persistent storage. for hosted, we can set deletion policies and certs but there's an attestation step. irreversible deletion uses secure overwrite schedules and we provide logs showing deletion events.
[07:24] [07:40] Daniel Cho: ok, curious about model artifact provenance — we need to show models were vetted. does Redwood maintain model manifests and hashing?
[07:48] Lena Park: yes — we keep immutable model manifests and hashes for performance profiles and we can share validation docs. for private, you can bring your own vetted model artifacts and we can sign them with your keys.
[08:05] Tom Alvarez: network topologies: if we run Private in our VPC, does Redwood need egress to the control plane? we want minimal cross-account egress.
[08:13] Marco Ruiz: we support either: a customer-managed control plane in your account (no egress) or a hybrid where the data plane is in your VPC and control plane discusses telemetry with Redwood's management plane over a secured tunnel. for strict setups we recommend full customer-managed control plane and an air-gapped option.
[08:36] Priya Singh: what about SAML assertion retention? we can't persist full assertions longer than 30 days.
[08:43] Marco Ruiz: typically we persist minimal auth metadata (user id, roles, token id) and not full assertions. full assertions are ephemeral and not stored unless you opt in.
[08:56] [09:10] Daniel Cho: any customers in logistics with similar constraints? helps our risk team.
[09:15] Lena Park: yes, a couple — we can provide redacted case studies and reference contacts under an NDA.
[09:22] Priya Singh: about encryption in transit: TLS versions, mutual TLS?
[09:27] Marco Ruiz: TLS 1.2+ supported, mutual TLS available for service-to-service in Private and Dedicated; hosted supports mTLS for customer endpoints via whitelisting.
[09:40] Tom Alvarez: we heard mention of token-level cost breakdowns and tracing — can that be restricted to certain users? we don't want devs seeing prod cost breakdowns.
[09:51] Marco Ruiz: yes — the console RBAC controls access to dashboards and cost views. you can restrict to finance or platform roles.
[10:05] [10:30] Priya Singh: encryption at rest standards? AES-GCM? FIPS?
[10:35] Marco Ruiz: AES-256 GCM for data at rest, FIPS-140-2 modules available when using HSMs that are FIPS validated. we'll note which builds are on FIPS stacks.
[10:50] Daniel Cho: what about forensic access? if we need to pull logs for a breach, how fast can we get a chain-of-custody export?
[10:59] Marco Ruiz: for Private it's immediate — you query your own log store. for Dedicated we can accelerate exports to your S3 and provide signed manifests. for hosted we'll coordinate and provide signed export packages, typically within SLA windows defined in enterprise contracts.
[11:20] [11:40] Priya Singh: regulatory: do you support data residency controls by region for stored embeddings and logs?
[11:47] Marco Ruiz: yes. we can pin model variants and storage to regions. embeddings storage can be configured to stay in-region for the dataset. for maximum assurance we recommend Private in-region.
[12:02] Tom Alvarez: about embedding retention — we want ephemeral embeddings for search use-cases and longer retention for analytics; can we configure per-route?
[12:12] Marco Ruiz: per-route retention is supported; you can set TTLs for caches and embeddings. ephemeral modes avoid writing to persistent stores.
[12:24] [12:40] Daniel Cho: governance: do you have SOC2 controls mapped to client-facing docs showing how each control is met?
[12:47] Lena Park: yes we'll share a controls mapping — how our controls map to SOC2 trust services criteria and ISO clauses.
[12:55] Priya Singh: logging format and SIEM compatibility?
[13:00] Marco Ruiz: JSON structured logs, support for Common Event Format, and customers push to Splunk/Datadog/Elastic. we also provide a schema doc for the fields.
[13:15] Tom Alvarez: question about model caching — are KV caches encrypted? if we wipe them, how do we prove it?
[13:22] Marco Ruiz: KV caches can be encrypted with local disk keys wrapped by KMS. we provide deletion logs and can generate retention/erase attestations for wipes as part of the design.
[13:40] [14:00] Daniel Cho: ok great. timeline: we have an internal procurement window in Q1 and need a pilot in December. cost will be a blocker if dedicated is too expensive. how flexible are pilot terms?
[14:10] Lena Park: pilots are usually a month with a small committed reserved capacity for Dedicated or a limited Private pilot. we can do a hosted proof-of-concept but with masked data; or Private pilot in your VPC. we'll follow up with options.
[14:28] Priya Singh: any certifications for personnel handling logs? background checks?
[14:33] Marco Ruiz: yes, we have personnel policies and background checks for staff with privileged access; details are in the SOC 2 pack.
[14:44] [15:00] Daniel Cho: on the legal side, data processing addendums and SCCs for cross-border — do you provide standard DPA templates?
[15:08] Lena Park: yes, we have DPA and SCCs; we'll include standard templates, and our legal is open to redlines for enterprise contracts.
[15:20] Tom Alvarez: one more: do you support token binding or ephemeral session tokens so leaked tokens can't be reused later?
[15:28] Marco Ruiz: we support short-lived tokens and token binding via mTLS and nonce checks; session tokens by default expire quickly and can be rotated programmatically.
[15:42] [16:00] Priya Singh: thinking about incident response: do you provide runbooks and playbooks for joint IR with customers?
[16:08] Marco Ruiz: yes, we have incident response playbooks and we run joint tabletop exercises with customers as an add-on.
[16:20] Daniel Cho: ok. let's talk costs briefly — what drives price differences between Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
[16:29] Lena Park: hosted is pay-as-you-go, good for dev and non-sensitive workloads. Dedicated is reserved GPUs with committed usage discounts and preferred latency SLOs. Private includes engineering and setup fees for VPC/on-prem plus infra costs — generally highest but gives you full control over keys and data residency.
[16:50] Marco Ruiz: also features like per-tenant KMS, HSM integrations, and private control plane are typically Private-only and can affect cost.
[17:02] [17:20] Priya Singh: can Redwood do hybrid? e.g., keep sensitive manifests in Private but route lower-sensitivity inference to hosted to save cost?
[17:29] Marco Ruiz: yes — smart routing can send requests by policy: latency, cost, data sensitivity tags, or tenant. we can fallback to hosted variants for non-sensitive queries.
[17:45] Daniel Cho: what's the SLA for Dedicated?
[17:50] Lena Park: Dedicated comes with uptime and latency SLOs in the enterprise contract — typical 99.9% availability and latency objectives, plus credits for missed SLOs. exact numbers in the quote.
[18:02] [18:20] Tom Alvarez: curious about rollback and version pins — if a model introduces regression, can we pin previous versions and audit who rolled?
[18:28] Marco Ruiz: yes — model versioning and rollout history are tracked; canary rollouts supported and audit logs show who deployed what.
[18:40] Priya Singh: any limitations on retention for legal hold? sometimes legal put data on hold beyond TTLs.
[18:48] Marco Ruiz: we support legal-hold flags to prevent deletion for specific artifacts, maintain chain-of-custody exports. this is for Dedicated/Private; hosted support through contractual terms.
[19:05] [19:30] Daniel Cho: ok, we're narrowing. priority for us: 1) SSO+SCIM 2) per-tenant CMKs + HSM 3) immutable, searchable audit logs 4) per-route retention 5) regional residency. if Redwood can show these, procurement looks favorable.
[19:50] Lena Park: perfect. we'll produce a technical appendix aligning each item to controls and architecture notes.
[20:05] Marco Ruiz: i'll draft a KMS integration note, HSM options, and a sample network diagram showing control/data plane separation.
[20:18] Priya Singh: one item — for embedded features where we do semantic search, do you allow us to encrypt vectors at rest with our keys?
[20:26] Marco Ruiz: yes, vector stores can be encrypted; we support envelope encryption and per-collection keys for vector stores.
[20:38] [21:00] Daniel Cho: what about tokenization of PII before sending to hosted models? do you provide SDKs or do we handle?
[21:08] Marco Ruiz: we provide client SDKs with hooks for redaction/tokenization; many customers build a pre-processing step in their pipeline to mask PII before hitting hosted endpoints.
[21:25] Priya Singh: last question — are retention policies enforceable in backups? we need deletion to propagate into backups too.
[21:33] Marco Ruiz: backups follow the same retention lifecycle; for Private you control the backup retention; for hosted we can provide deletion attestations including backups within agreed windows.
[21:50] [22:10] Daniel Cho: alright. can we get an estimate for a 3-week pilot that covers 6 GPU nodes, HSM integration, and per-tenant audit logging?
[22:20] Lena Park: yes — marco will size it and i'll follow up with pricing.
[22:28] Marco Ruiz: i'll put together two options: Private pilot in-VPC (higher infra work) and Dedicated pilot with encrypted logs shipped to your S3 for audit (lower setup time).
[22:44] Priya Singh: please also include expected lead times for HSM connector config — we have CloudHSM but want to know if Redwood needs custom drivers.
[22:54] Marco Ruiz: usually connectors are standard, but i'll list edge cases and any driver work.
[23:08] [23:30] Daniel Cho: can you send a redacted reference from another logistics customer? procurement will ask.
[23:36] Lena Park: yes, NDA or redacted case study — we'll include it.
[23:44] Priya Singh: for the pilot, can we have a baked-in deletion test where you show us deletion logs and a signed attestation?
[23:52] Marco Ruiz: absolutely — we can schedule a deletion attestation run during the pilot.
[24:05] [24:30] Daniel Cho: ok, next steps?
[24:35] Lena Park: recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO docs + pentest summary, marco will share KMS/HSM integration note and pilot sizing/cost by 2026-11-02, i'll send a draft commercial/quote and DPA, and Priya/Tom will send retention categories and residency constraints by 2026-11-06.
[24:58] Priya Singh: agreed. also please add a calendar invite for the HSM deep dive week of 2026-11-09.
[25:08] Lena Park: will do.
[25:14] [25:30] Daniel Cho: excellent. anything else from Redwood?
[25:35] Marco Ruiz: nothing else from me — i'll add the network diagram and sample syslog schema.
[25:42] Lena Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[25:48] Priya Singh: thanks all.
[25:52] Tom Alvarez: thanks.
[26:00] [END — recording stopped]

Call notes: The conversation leaned heavy on Private deployment needs (HSM/KMS, data residency) but team is open to Dedicated for faster pilot. The customer requested formal attestations, a KMS integration dossier, and a pilot costing. Action owners listed above.
